_note: ChatSOP's TinyAgent layer (over TinyAgent/config.default.json and ~/.tinyagent/config.json). Owner rules: clients name a tier, never a model; every model call of the project goes through the TinyAgent server (node TinyAgent/bin/tinyagent.mjs serve, port 18080). Keys: ~/.tinyagent/keys/<provider>.env. Paths are relative to the repository root (baseDir).

local._note: tiny (owner decision 2026-10-03, MoE A/B of experiments/proposal/structure-and-formalizer-models.md section 9): Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M (MoE, about 3B active), always on: started with the TinyAgent server (startAtBoot) and restarted on demand; GPU reservation lock files block a start. 8 slots of 16k tokens, as the server ran before TinyAgent (measured: about 66 tokens/s for one request, 118 tokens/s aggregate at 4 busy slots, 22.8 GB GPU memory; with 8 busy slots each request drops below 20 tokens/s).

localsuper._note: micro (formerly supertiny, owner 2026-10-03): Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 Q4_K_M, on demand, stopped after 15 idle minutes, 32 slots.

localnano._note: nano (owner 2026-10-03): the official Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 GGUF (Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF), on demand, stopped after 15 idle minutes, 32 slots.

tiers._note: owner 2026-10-02: clients and jobs name a tier, never a concrete model. A tier is a chain of {upstream, model}; the first usable entry serves, the rest is its fallback. best is unconfigured (pro models via OpenRouter later): a request for it is an error. equivalence (owner 2026-10-03): a very small, fast model that only decides whether two short answers are equivalent (A implies B and B implies A); today the local Qwen3-4B, no fallback; used only after deterministic normalization fails. structure and formalizer (owner 2026-10-03): the PSM (GLiNER2.5 base, POST /v1/structure) and the LFM (T5-base NL-to-FOL, POST /v1/fol) on the local small-model service; JSON endpoints, not chat; no fallback. Owner 2026-10-03: the backends of structure and formalizer are swappable: structure and formalizer name one of the variant tiers below; a variant with `prompt` is a chat model with a role prompt (prompts/<name>.md, TinyAgent/lib/prompted.mjs) under the same JSON contract: structure-gliner (GLiNER2.5), structure-tiny (Qwen3-4B + psm-v1), formalizer-t5 (T5-base), formalizer-t5-3b (T5-3B), formalizer-tiny (Qwen3-4B + fol-v1), formalizer-llama-fol (Llama-3.2-1B NL2FOL + fol-plain-v1). MoE A/B (owner 2026-10-03): tiny-moe-qwen (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) with structure-moe-qwen and formalizer-moe-qwen under the same role prompts; an on-demand local upstream (exclusiveGroup ondemand), no fallback; kept pending the owner's decision on the A/B (Nemotron and the small thinking models lost and were removed). Control (owner 2026-10-03): structure-good and formalizer-good, the good tier's model (deepseek-v4.1-flash, cloud) under the same role prompts with reasoning (effort medium, 32k budget), to separate a weak model from a limit of the method or the converters. Owner decision 2026-10-03 (MoE A/B, section 9 of experiments/proposal/structure-and-formalizer-models.md): tiny is Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on the always-on upstream local (fallback medium's deepseek-v4-flash); supertiny is the former tiny Qwen3-4B on the on-demand upstream localsuper (fallback tiny, then medium's model); equivalence names supertiny; structure-tiny and formalizer-tiny (and thus structure and formalizer) run on the MoE, structure-supertiny and formalizer-supertiny keep the 4B variants; the *-moe-qwen names are aliases of the tiny variants. FOL repair (owner 2026-10-03): the prompted formalizer tiers use fol-v2 (the constructs the converter of lib/formalize/fol now reads: disjunctive and IFF conclusions, universal conditions, value rules, comparisons as conditions, unknowns with Integer/Maximize/Minimize, pow); fol-v1 stays for replaying earlier runs. Owner 2026-10-03: use the openference plan more: medium = openference DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (plan, 0.75 credit/call), OpenRouter as fallback. openference DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Kimi K2.6 are billed from a credit balance, not the plan; good stays on OpenRouter deepseek-v4.1-flash. Owner 2026-10-03: openference everywhere, OpenRouter only as fallback: good = openference GLM-5.3 (plan, 2 credits/call), fallback OpenRouter deepseek-v4.1-flash. Metacognition (owner 2026-10-03): formalizer names formalizer-tiny-v3, the tiny model under fol-v3 (fol-v2 plus options as SUPPOSE, ASSUME, and the questions Effect, Explain, Missing, Why, Change, Assumed that the converter lowers to candidate wires and mode effect/abduce/why_not/explain); formalizer-tiny keeps fol-v2 for replays. A/B in wire-type-proposals.md P-1. Owner 2026-10-03 (TinyAgent): nano = local Qwen3-0.6B; micro = the former supertiny Qwen3-4B (supertiny stays an alias during the migration); best is served by tiny until a pro model is configured. Owner 2026-10-03 (fol-v3 agent's finding): GLM-5.3 ignored max_tokens and reasoned for up to 20 minutes per call; owner decision 2026-10-03 evening: good = openference DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (plan, 0.75 credit/call), fallback OpenRouter deepseek-v4.1-flash; structure-good and formalizer-good follow. The good entries keep a duration cap (timeoutMs 290000): a runaway call is cut, reported as upstream_timeout, never cached, and falls back down the chain. Fix 2026-10-03 (phase 2): the OpenRouter DeepSeek entries reason by default and spent a short question's budget (max_tokens 8) thinking, so the fallbacks of tiny, small, medium and good answered cut and empty (budget_exhausted at 8 tokens); a chain entry's extraBody now fills the request fields the caller did not set, and these entries carry reasoning off (a caller that asks for reasoning still gets it).

fallback._note: owner 2026-10-02: when openference is unavailable (unreachable or 5xx after retry.max5xx retries, 429 after retry.max retries or with retry-after above maxWaitMs, or a queue/plan-gate wait above maxWaitMs) a request for a mapped model goes to this upstream and model. Response header x-tinyagent-fallback; opt out per request with x-tinyagent-no-fallback: 1.

compare._note: USD per 1M tokens. DeepSeek official prices from https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing (read 2026-10-02): deepseek-flash (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) cache hit 0.006/0.003, cache miss 0.30/0.15, output 1.20/0.60 at peak/off-peak (off-peak is half; peak 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC on weekdays). Re-check before deciding.

policy._note: owner 2026-10-02: LLM batch work runs as registered jobs (the TinyAgent job runner) with a budget per run; requests carry x-tinyagent-purpose. Allowed purposes pass; any other request (no purpose or an unknown one) counts against a small daily allowance and is refused beyond it (403 untagged_limit). A registered run is refused at its budget (402 budget_exceeded) and after it finished (403 run_finished).

interactive._note: owner 2026-10-02: a person waiting (chat turn, formalization, answer wording) goes first in every upstream queue and falls back down its tier chain after maxWaitMs instead of queueing behind batch jobs

background._note: owner 2026-10-03: background work (header x-tinyagent-priority: background, a job's "priority": "background", or a purpose listed here) runs only when nothing else waits and, on a plan provider, only while the plan keeps 30% of its rate and quota windows free for interactive and normal work; it is held, never refused.

cache._note: owner 2026-10-02: responses are cached by default (the same request gets the same answer; the reasoner reacts to context changes, the formalization need not vary). Key = the whole request body + target tier/upstream + model identity (local GGUF size and mtime). Header x-tinyagent-cache: off | use | strict (a miss is refused, for regressions) | record. Only complete non-streamed 200 answers from the tier's first model are stored. Dir ~/.tinyagent/cache/.

runner._note: The job runner of ChatSOP: run folders under state/llm-jobs/ (gitignored); the task template library jobs/templates/; roles (owner 2026-10-02): planner and decider good, auditor medium, worker small, worker-short tiny.

lambdas._note: ChatSOP's TaskLambdas (jobs/lambdas/: chatsop.mjs formalize, chat-batch; regression.mjs regression-record, regression-reference, regression-grow, regression-argument, the offline formalization regression of 2026-10-03, cloud tiers at background priority) and its job folders as TaskLambdas; the task templates of jobs/templates/ are TaskLambdas too. Their model calls carry the purpose lambda:<name>.
